column3: “A shout of battle” is rendered “a trumpet blast of war.”
“Among the walls” is rendered “inside the walls.”
“Why do you boast” is rendered “How boastful you are,” and “apostate” as “backsliding.”
“Turn back the captivity” is rendered “restore the fortunes.”
“Corrupted” is rendered “decayed,” and NASB supplies “good” and “their.”
“Make deep to dwell” is rendered “dwell in the depths.”
“I will strip” is rendered as past, “I have stripped.”
“A waste” is rendered “an object of horror.”
“I will make” is rendered as past, “I have made.”
“Horror your” is rendered “As for the terror of you”; the meaning is uncertain.
NASB supplies “one will come up” and “against.”
“Someone will ascend” is rendered “He will mount up.”
“In the sea” is rendered “by the sea”; the text is difficult.
NASB keeps the Hebrew “not” (“has not been deserted”), which some versions omit.
